s1.syndrome_frame: a gradually enlarging, red, cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule on the upper arm
salient_findings: red tumor on the right upper arm
key_facts: 16-year-old girl
previously healthy
lesion started as a small cutaneous nodule
enlarged over 6 months
no history of local trauma or insect bite
personal, past, and family histories unremarkable
6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red tumor
nontender, firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor
normal laboratory tests
multilocular spaces below the epidermis on pathological examination
solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance

shortlist.label: Pilomatrixoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical description of a firm, cutaneous nodule with a chalky-white cut surface

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with a gradually enlarging, protuberant tumor

shortlist.label: Cylindroma
shortlist.why_kept: possible given the multilocular spaces and solid tumor on pathological examination

shortlist.label: Trichoepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of a cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: a possible diagnosis given the rapid growth and cutaneous location of the tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis, along with the description of a solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance, is characteristic of pilomatrixoma.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma typically presents as a solitary, firm, and dome-shaped nodule with a central crater, which does not match the described multilocular spaces and solid tumor with a chalky-white cut surface.
